# Health

Applies when the change touches: clinical or patient data, medical devices. Every role loads this pack for the steps it works in, on top of its own playbook. The test commands below are best practices the gate runs: put them in the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`, so a red one blocks the merge. Name the pack in the Spec's Context; it does not count against a Task's `skills`.

## Standards

| Standard | Edition | Checked | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules | 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164, current | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C> |
| HL7 FHIR | R4 4.0.1, or R5 where adopted | 2026-09-28 | <https://hl7.org/fhir/> |
| IEC 62304 for medical device software | 2006 + A1:2015 | 2026-09-28 | <https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/22794> |
| ISO 14971 risk management | 2019 | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.iso.org/standard/72704.html> |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item |
| --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd next`) | Clinical or patient data is privacy and compliance: major, the privacy and compliance pools, a DPIA or HIPAA risk analysis. |
| Specify | Minimum necessary data; access logging; FHIR resources and profiles named; the safety class for device software (IEC 62304). |
| Implement | PHI encrypted in transit and at rest; an audit log for every access; no PHI in logs, fixtures, or prompts. |
| Review | The hazard analysis (ISO 14971) is updated for the change; requirements trace to tests. |
| Ship | Access-log anomalies and the error rate on clinical paths are rollback triggers; the incident reporting path is known. |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FHIR validation | every produced resource validates against its profile | the HL7 FHIR validator in the test commands |
| PHI scan | no PHI in logs, fixtures, or outputs | Presidio or an equivalent scanner |
| Access-control tests | each role sees only its records | tests per role and per record |
| Traceability check | every requirement has a test | a traceability matrix check for device software |
| Dependency and container scanning | no high finding | OSV-Scanner or Trivy |

## Keep it current

A standard marked emerging is a draft, a first edition, or a young practice: apply it only when the change clearly needs it, and say so in the Spec. A standard checked more than a year ago is stale: `aidd eval standards` lists it, and the loop contract's research-first rule applies. When the change needs a standard this pack lacks, look up the authoritative source, record the edition in the Spec's Context, and propose the update to the aidd project's roles registry (`schemas/roles.json` in the aidd repository) as an improvement.
